title: [PDF] MITOCHONDRIA AND AGING
abstract: THE ROLE OF MITOCHONDRIA IN AGING Oxidative damage Among the byproducts of ­ mitochondrial energy production are “reactive oxygen species” that include hydrogen peroxide—the same hydrogen peroxide used as an antiseptic and hair bleach. Using this assay on aging ­ human brain cells, they found a mixed array of rearranged DNAs. The technique should have wider ­ applications, as scientists seek to pinpoint defects and mutations in mitochondrial DNA that might be the result of oxidative damage. THE ROLE OF MITOCHONDRIA IN AGE-RELATED DISEASE The first disease-causing ­ mutations in mitochondrial DNA were reported in 1988; today researchers have ­ identified more than 50 such mutations. In ­ addition to mitochondrial DNA damage, diseases can also ­ originate from oxidant ­ damage to proteins and lipids in the ­ mitochondria itself.
